analysis.title: US Autos & Industrial Tech: October US auto SAAR was in the mid-to-high 15 mn range
key_insights: October US light vehicle SAAR was about 15.7 mn per Motor Intelligence and 15.5 mn per Wards, below the StreetAccount consensus of 15.9 mn. September 2026 SAAR was about 16.0 mn and October 2025 was about 15.7 mn per Wards.

October was the first month with SAAR below 16 mn since February. GS expects this to feed the investor debate over whether the market softens in a more material and sustained way on inflation and rates pressure.

GS base case is that SAAR stays stable and relatively flat in 2027. It cites absolute units still growing yoy in October (about 1% yoy adjusted for selling days), GS auto leading indicators, and healthy inventory.

Absolute units were about 1.34 mn in October vs 1.33 mn in September and 1.28 mn in October 2025 per Motor Intelligence, mid-single-digit yoy growth unadjusted. October 2026 had 1 more selling day than October 2025 and 3 more than September 2026.
By segment, car sales were up about 2% yoy, pickups up about 1% and SUVs up about 6%. SUV share of units rose to 58.8% from 57.6% and pickup share fell to 19.9% from 20.6%.
Ford sales were about flat yoy and GM sales were up about 1% per Motor Intelligence. Ford market share fell to 12.9% from 13.6% and GM share fell to 16.6% from 17.1%.

In large pickups, GM share fell to 36.4% from 38.8% a year ago (37.3% in September). Ford share rose to 35.5% from 33.3% (33.7% in September). Stellantis share fell to 18.8% from 19.7% (20.1% in September).

F-Series sales were up 8% yoy, GM full-size pickups down 5% and Stellantis full-size pickups down 3%. GS says Ford's yoy gain may reflect recovery from about 100K units of 2025 production lost to the Novelis fire, and GM's decline likely reflects the model year refresh starting 4Q26.

EV sales were up about 15% yoy and hybrids up about 30% yoy per Motor Intelligence. EV mix was about 6.3% of sales vs about 5.7% a year ago. GS notes the EV data carries more estimation because Tesla does not report monthly or US-specific sales.
Tesla sales were up 8% yoy, with Model Y up 23%, Model 3 down 20% and Cybertruck up 44%. Ford E-Transit fell 55% and Mach-E fell 57%. GM Lyriq fell 39%, Equinox EV fell 82% and Blazer EV fell 53%.
Rivian sales were estimated up 95% yoy, with R1S down 30%, R1T down 14%, EDV up 171%, and some R2 sales against none a year ago.
Incentive spending per vehicle was about $3,493, up 8% yoy and 4% sequentially.

Finished vehicle inventory rose to about 2,826K units in October from about 2,709K in September, still modestly below the historical 3 mn+ range. Industry days of inventory was 59 vs 51 in September and 60 a year ago. Pickup DOI was 84, SUV 55 and car 45.

sector_views.rationale: GS base case is a stable, relatively flat SAAR in 2027 despite the October miss vs consensus, supported by unit growth, leading indicators and healthy inventory.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Below the 15.9 mn StreetAccount consensus and below September's 16.0 mn.
Compares with about 16.0 mn in September 2026 and about 15.7 mn in October 2025.

tension_points.bull_case: GS base case is that SAAR stays stable and relatively flat in 2027. Absolute units still grew yoy in October (about 1% adjusted for selling days), auto leading indicators are supportive, and inventory is healthy.
tension_points.bear_case: October SAAR missed the 15.9 mn consensus and was the first month below 16 mn since February. Investors debate whether inflation and rates pressure will soften the market in a material and sustained way. Days of inventory rose to 59 from 51 and incentives rose 4% sequentially.

theme_stances.key_argument: GS base case is that SAAR remains stable and relatively flat in 2027, consistent with continued unit growth, leading indicators and healthy inventory.
theme_stances.evidence: our base case view remains that SAAR will remain stable
